humanoid.description: An upright biped. Axes run -1 to 1 with 0 neutral, unless noted. Every combination of these values is guaranteed to produce a valid body; a reader that clamps out-of-range values to the stated bounds will always be able to build one.

height.description: Standing height in millimetres. Extreme builds may exceed this slightly, since a body that cannot be constructed is worse than one a little off its nominal stature.

build.description: Overall mass, from slight to heavy. Thousandths, -1000 to 1000.

shoulderWidth.description: Width of the shoulder girdle. Thousandths, -1000 to 1000.

hipWidth.description: Width of the pelvis. Thousandths, -1000 to 1000.

limbLength.description: Limb length relative to the torso. Longer limbs raise the pelvis and so shorten the torso at a fixed stature. Thousandths, -1000 to 1000.

extremitySize.description: Hand and foot size. Thousandths, -1000 to 1000.

quadruped.description: A four-legged creature. Axes run -1 to 1 with 0 neutral, unless noted.

height.description: Height of the back line in millimetres.

bodyLength.description: Body length from shoulder to hip. Thousandths, -1000 to 1000.

build.description: Overall mass, from slight to heavy. Thousandths, -1000 to 1000.

legLength.description: Legginess. Longer legs slim the body at a fixed back height. Thousandths, -1000 to 1000.

skin.description: A body's complexion. Axes are thousandths, as elsewhere: the AT Protocol data model has no floating-point type. Every combination is a usable complexion.

melanin.description: Base depth of tone, from palest to deepest. Thousandths, 0 to 1000.

undertone.description: Hue beneath the tone: -1000 cool and pink, +1000 warm and olive.

blush.description: How much blood shows through at cheeks, ears, and knuckles. Thousandths, 0 to 1000.

stubble.description: Stubble across the lower face. Thousandths, 0 to 1000.

eyes.description: How a body's eyes are shaped and set. Axes are thousandths, as elsewhere: the AT Protocol data model has no floating-point type. Eyes are geometry that moves rather than a painted feature, so these place a globe and the lids that close over it.

size.description: Eye size, as a fraction of the head's radius. Thousandths, 0 to 1000.

spacing.description: How far apart the eyes are set: -1000 close, +1000 wide.

depth.description: How deeply the eyes are set: -1000 protruding, +1000 sunken.

aperture.description: How far open the lids rest: 0 shut, 1000 wide.

hair.description: The hair grown on a body's head, as strand groups swept over the scalp. Axes are thousandths, as elsewhere: the AT Protocol data model has no floating-point type. A reader that clamps out-of-range values to the stated bounds will always be able to grow hair.

length.description: How far the hair falls: 0 cropped, 1000 past the shoulder blades. The fringe over the brow is always short, whatever this says.

volume.description: How far the hair stands off the scalp: -1000 flat, +1000 full.

coverage.description: Where the hairline sits: -1000 receding, +1000 low on the brow.

part.description: Where the parting runs: -1000 over the left ear, +1000 over the right.

wave.description: How much the hair waves as it falls: 0 straight, 1000 curling.

shade.description: Colour along a melanin ramp: 0 black, 1000 pale blonde.

groups.description: How many strand groups to grow. Costs geometry, so it is bounded; readers may lower it for distant or low-end rendering without changing the record.

outfit.description: What a body is wearing. Close-fitting garments are cut from the body's own surface a few millimetres outside it, so they fit any wearer without being re-cut and cannot intersect the body. Colour axes are thousandths, as elsewhere: the AT Protocol data model has no floating-point type.

sleeve.description: How far down the arm the top's sleeves run. Named for where the hem lands, not for a tailoring term: a cut follows the body's zones and an arm carries two of them, so 'forearm' ends about 70% of the way down and 'wrist' at 93%. Readers that do not recognise a value should fall back to 'forearm'.

leg.description: How far down the leg the trousers run. As with the sleeve, named for where the hem lands: the middle cut finishes below the knee rather than at it. Readers that do not recognise a value should fall back to 'ankle'.

topHue.description: The top's colour around the wheel. Thousandths, 0 to 1000.

topShade.description: How light the top is. Thousandths, 0 to 1000.

legHue.description: The trousers' colour around the wheel. Thousandths, 0 to 1000.

legShade.description: How light the trousers are. Thousandths, 0 to 1000.
